name: qra_nist
description: QRA generation for NIST 800-53/800-171/DISA STIG controls applied to F-36 program

input.name: AC-2 Account Management — F-36 ALIS
input.description: Account management controls for F-36 Autonomic Logistics Information System

cases.source_text: The F-36 ALIS system enforces account management through automated provisioning tied to unit manning rosters. Service accounts for depot-level maintenance terminals require dual authorization from both the system administrator and the maintenance officer. Privileged accounts accessing avionics diagnostic data are reviewed quarterly per NIST AC-2(3) requirements. DISA STIG V-219200 mandates that all ALIS privileged access sessions be logged with tamper-evident audit trails. Temporary accounts for contractor personnel at the Fort Worth plant expire after 90 days unless explicitly renewed by the Information System Security Officer.
cases.notes: Must reference ALIS system, not generic AC-2 definition

input.name: SI-7 Software and Firmware Integrity — F-36 OFP Build
input.description: Integrity verification for F-36 Operational Flight Program software builds

cases.source_text: The F-36 Operational Flight Program (OFP) build pipeline implements software integrity verification per NIST SI-7 at three stages: pre-compilation hash validation of source modules, post-compilation binary signature verification using PKI certificates rooted in the program's HSM, and deployment-time integrity checks on the mission data loader. DISA STIG V-219181 requires that all OFP binaries be signed with FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules. The F135 engine FADEC firmware follows a separate integrity chain managed by the engine vendor, with hash verification at the depot level only — no field-level integrity checking is currently implemented, creating a potential gap in SI-7 compliance.
cases.notes: Should identify the FADEC firmware integrity gap

input.name: SC-7 Boundary Protection — F-36 Plant Network
input.description: Network boundary protection at F-36 manufacturing facility

cases.source_text: The Fort Worth F-36 assembly plant maintains boundary protection per NIST SC-7 through a multi-tier network architecture. The industrial control network (SCADA/PLC segments) is air-gapped from the enterprise IT network with data diodes for one-way telemetry transfer. ALIS terminals in maintenance bays connect via a dedicated VLAN with firewall rules restricting traffic to the central ALIS server cluster. Building 7 expansion terminals were provisioned with temporary unrestricted VLAN access during construction — the temporary bypass was never revoked, creating a SC-7 compliance gap. DISA STIG V-219151 requires annual boundary assessment documentation, which has not been updated since the Building 7 expansion.
cases.notes: Building 7 compliance gap is the key finding

input.name: AU-6 Audit Record Review — F-36 SIEM Integration
input.description: Audit log review and SIEM integration for F-36 systems

cases.source_text: F-36 program audit record review per NIST AU-6 is implemented through centralized SIEM integration. All ALIS, mission planning, and avionics diagnostic systems forward audit logs to the program's Splunk deployment. Automated correlation rules detect anomalous maintenance activity patterns — specifically, after-hours OFP modification attempts trigger immediate alerts to the ISSO. DISA STIG V-219201 mandates that audit logs be reviewed within 24 hours for privileged access events. Current compliance rate for 24-hour review is 73%, with the remaining 27% delayed due to staffing shortfalls at deployed units. CCI-001914 requires that the organization employs automated mechanisms to integrate audit record review, analysis, and reporting.
cases.notes: 73% compliance rate is a key metric to reference

input.name: IA-2 Multi-Factor Authentication — F-36 Remote Access
input.description: MFA enforcement for remote maintenance access to F-36 systems

cases.source_text: Remote access to F-36 maintenance systems requires multi-factor authentication per NIST IA-2(1) and IA-2(2). Depot-level technicians accessing ALIS remotely use CAC/PIV smart cards combined with PIN entry. The VPN concentrator at Fort Worth enforces certificate-based mutual TLS before granting network access. DISA STIG V-219170 verifies MFA enforcement on all remote sessions. Field units at deployed locations use RSA SecurID tokens as an alternative when CAC infrastructure is unavailable — this creates a IA-2(12) gap as the token-based authentication does not meet the NIST requirement for a cryptographic authenticator.
cases.notes: RSA SecurID gap for deployed units is key finding

input.name: CM-3 Configuration Change Control — F-36 OFP Releases
input.description: Configuration change control for F-36 operational flight program updates

cases.source_text: F-36 OFP configuration change control per NIST CM-3 follows a four-gate process: change request board approval, regression test suite execution in the software integration lab (SIL), independent verification and validation (IV&V), and production deployment authorization from the Chief Engineer. All changes are tracked in the F-36 Configuration Status Accounting database with full audit trail. Emergency changes (safety-critical defect corrections) bypass the change board but require post-facto review within 72 hours per DISA STIG V-219182. The average OFP release cycle is 18 months, with critical patches averaging 6 weeks from identification to deployment — the 6-week window represents a period of known vulnerability exposure.
cases.notes: 6-week vulnerability window is the key risk

input.name: PE-3 Physical Access Control — F-36 Clean Room
input.description: Physical access controls for F-36 avionics clean room and SCIF

cases.source_text: Physical access to the F-36 avionics clean room and SCIF at the Fort Worth facility is controlled per NIST PE-3 with biometric door locks (iris scan), escort requirements for visitors, and continuous CCTV monitoring. All personnel entering the clean room must badge through a mantrap with tailgating detection. The SCIF enforces two-person integrity for accessing classified avionics design data. DISA STIG V-219190 requires physical access logs to be retained for one year and correlated with logical access events. Current gap: the loading dock adjacent to the clean room uses legacy proximity cards (HID Prox) that are vulnerable to cloning — upgrade to iCLASS SE has been approved but not yet implemented.
cases.notes: HID Prox cloning vulnerability is the key gap

input.name: SA-12 Supply Chain Protection — F-36 Vendor Components
input.description: Supply chain risk management for F-36 vendor-supplied components

cases.source_text: F-36 supply chain protection per NIST SA-12 addresses counterfeit component detection and vendor integrity verification. All avionics LRUs and mission computer boards undergo X-ray inspection and decapsulation testing at receiving. The F135 engine FADEC firmware is supplied by the engine vendor with digital signatures, but the signing key rotation policy is managed by the vendor — the program office has no independent verification capability. DISA STIG coverage for supply chain is limited: no V-ID checks currently address firmware supply chain integrity for vendor-managed subsystems. This creates a critical gap where the highest-value target (engine control firmware) has the weakest verification chain.
cases.notes: FADEC firmware vendor dependency is the critical gap

input.name: AC-6 Least Privilege — F-36 ALIS Role Model
input.description: Least privilege implementation in F-36 ALIS role-based access

cases.source_text: The F-36 ALIS implements least privilege per NIST AC-6 through a seven-tier role model: read-only viewer, flight line technician, depot maintainer, mission planner, system administrator, ISSO, and program office administrator. Each role maps to specific ALIS functional modules — flight line technicians can view and update maintenance records but cannot access mission data or avionics diagnostic tools. Privileged roles (system administrator, ISSO) require separate administrative accounts distinct from daily-use accounts per AC-6(2). DISA STIG V-219202 verifies that no single account has combined maintenance and administrative privileges. Current issue: the 'depot maintainer' role was granted OFP upload permissions during a surge maintenance period and the elevated permissions were never revoked.
cases.notes: Depot maintainer permission creep is the finding

input.name: CP-9 System Backup — F-36 Mission Data
input.description: System backup and recovery for F-36 mission planning data

cases.source_text: F-36 mission planning data backup per NIST CP-9 follows a 3-2-1 strategy: three copies, two different media types, one offsite. Daily incremental backups of ALIS mission data are written to encrypted tape and transported to the offsite vault. Full backups occur weekly with integrity verification via SHA-256 checksums. Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for ALIS mission planning is 4 hours; Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is 24 hours. Testing of backup restoration occurs quarterly. Last quarterly test revealed that 12% of tape backups failed integrity verification due to degraded tape media — the program switched to LTO-9 but legacy LTO-7 tapes from 2024-2025 remain in the vault with unknown integrity status.
cases.notes: Legacy tape integrity gap is the key finding

notes.problem_statement: Jennifer Cheung persona needs QRAs grounded in F-36 datalake content through NIST/STIG lens, not abstract NIST definitions
notes.prompt_goal: Generate synthesis questions about how NIST controls apply to specific F-36 systems, identifying compliance gaps
